summary: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and Heidelberg University. He held positions at Fergusson College, Savitribai Phule Pune University as Director, and the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute as Secretary.

Ramesh Chandra Majumdar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at institutions including Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, he taught at the University of Calcutta and the University of Chicago, and chaired the History of Bengal Publication Committee.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. In 1967, he headed the Department of History and Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and was a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest University, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State University.
Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where he was supervised by Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina.

Ramkrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai, and the University of Göttingen, learning under Martin Haug. He held professorships at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and Elphinstone College.
Ramón Prats is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. He held posts at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources, attested in 1999, and Pompeu Fabra University, attested in 2017.
Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied under Steven D. Goodman and completed his doctoral work under the supervision of Richard K. Payne.

Rangama Chandawimala specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin and co-supervisor Kakkapalliye Anuruddha, and also studied with traditional teacher Attaragama Gnanawimala.

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Tai Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Kalu Rinpoche, and taught numerous students, including Chögyam Trungpa and Reginald A. Ray.

Raniero Gnoli worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. A student of Giuseppe Tucci, he served on the faculty at Sapienza University of Rome from approximately 1964 to 2000 and taught scholars including Raffaele Torella and Cristina Pecchia.
Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He has held an appointment as a professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz, attested in 2003 and 2017.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh was an Indologist and historian who studied at Fergusson College and under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Ancient Indian History at Gujarat Vidyapith and as Secretary of Gujarat Puratattva Mandir.

Rasmus Rask was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from 1807 to 1811 and later served there from 1825 to 1832 as Professor of Literary History and Librarian.

Ravindra Singh Bisht is a scholar of archaeology and Indology. He studied at the University of Lucknow from 1963 to 1967 and later served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India between 1969 and 2004.
Rawi Bhavilai was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Adelaide from 1960 to 1962. He later served as Director at Chulalongkorn University, attested in 2002.

Rebecca Redwood French is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Washington and Yale University. She has held academic posts at the University of Colorado Boulder and as Professor of Law at the University at Buffalo.

Regbi Pubaev was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University, he held posts at Buryat State University and the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies.

Reginald A. Ray works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Mircea Eliade and Chögyam Trungpa, and has held posts as a teacher at the University of Colorado Boulder and Professor in Buddhist Studies at Naropa University.
Rei Yoshimura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. He completed his studies at Waseda University between 1949 and 1954 and later served there as a professor from 1974 to 1999.

Reiko Ohnuma specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, and held posts at the University of Texas at Austin, the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.
